resultClassByDerivation.note: Normative conclusions are obligation_satisfied and obligation_violation. condition_not_met is a diagnostic activation result emitted BY a normative conditional rule; it is not itself a normative conclusion and never counts toward compliance.

normativeOutcomes.definition: The rule applied, required input and evidence were available, the evaluator executed successfully, and the normative invariant held.
As above, but the normative invariant was not satisfied.
No reliable compliance conclusion can be drawn. Never a pass and never a violation.
preconditions: evidence missing, conflicting, insufficient, or untrusted
or applicability cannot be safely determined

normativeOutcomes.definition: The evaluator could not execute correctly because of a programming, configuration, schema, dependency, or runtime problem. A defect in the evaluator, not a finding about the audited product.
preconditions: evaluator raised or failed to execute

normativeOutcomes.definition: An approved applicability predicate establishes that the obligation does not apply.

proxyResults.definition: The proxy condition held. This says nothing about whether the source obligation it stands in for was satisfied.
The proxy condition did not hold. This is not a product finding and is not an obligation violation.
The proxy condition could not be evaluated.
preconditions: required declared content absent or conflicting

proxyResults.definition: The proxy evaluator could not execute correctly.
preconditions: evaluator raised or failed to execute

preconditionResults.definition: The evaluator input was obtained. This is not an obligation outcome.
The evaluator input was not obtained. This is an input problem, never a product finding.
The precondition evaluator could not execute correctly.
preconditions: evaluator raised or failed to execute

notApplicableReachability: not_applicable is currently unreachable by every pilot rule. It may be assigned only when an approved applicability predicate evaluates false, and every pilot rule carries applicability.predicateApproved = false. It is retained so that evidence absence can never be routed to it; absence yields indeterminate.
prohibitedConflations: Missing evidence must never be reported as obligation_violation.
Evaluator failure must never be reported as a product finding or obligation_violation.
not_applicable must never be inferred from absence of evidence; only an approved applicability predicate may establish it.
indeterminate must never be counted as a passing rule.
obligation_satisfied must never be assigned when any required input, evidence, or provenance approval is missing; that case is indeterminate.
A proxy result must never be reported as satisfying or violating the source obligation it stands in for.
proxy_condition_met must never be converted into obligation_satisfied without separately approved bridge authority.
proxy_condition_not_met must never be converted into obligation_violation without separately approved bridge authority.
A precondition result must never be reported as an obligation outcome; an evaluator input is not a normative obligation.
Proxy and precondition results must never count as source-derived coverage.
A false antecedent must never be reported as obligation_satisfied; that would imply the consequence was fulfilled when it was never activated.
condition_not_met must never be counted toward normative compliance totals.
condition_not_met must never be conflated with indeterminate: the first means the condition was evaluated and did not hold, the second means it could not be evaluated.
vacuousSatisfactionPolicy: Vacuous satisfaction is not used. When a conditional rule's antecedent is false the result is condition_not_met, a diagnostic activation result rather than a normative conclusion. It carries countsAsObligationCompliance false, so it can never inflate compliance totals, and it is distinct from indeterminate, which means the antecedent could not be evaluated at all.

diagnosticActivationResults.definition: Emitted by a normative conditional rule when its antecedent was evaluated on trusted evidence and did not hold, so the conditional consequence was never activated. This is a diagnostic activation result, not a normative conclusion: it asserts nothing about whether the obligation was fulfilled.
preconditions: the antecedent was evaluated on trusted evidence
